01-play.speaker: GLaDOS
01-play.text: Your assistant has arrived, Gramps. Try not to lower the average intelligence on this side of the arena.

20-play.speaker: Saitama
20-play.text: Point me at the strongest one. I'll finish this before it gets complicated. After that, I'm going home, unless somebody knows a good discount store nearby. I'm not being rude. I just have errands, and the monsters can wait.

02-entrance.speaker: Po
02-entrance.text: Oh! You're Rick Gramps, right? The guy collecting fighters from different worlds? That's actually kind of amazing. Also kind of alarming. If you're looking for somebody who can handle a little pressure, I'm your panda. Just don't point me at anything with lasers.

02-defeat.speaker: Po
02-defeat.text: Okay, you got me. That was a real fight, and I'm saying that as somebody who has been punched through several walls. I'll join your collection, Gramps. But we train before breakfast, and I'm keeping the dumplings. Those are non-negotiable.

02-loss.speaker: Po
02-loss.text: Wow. That did not go the way I rehearsed it in my head. Your fighters are tough, but tough is not enough yet. Go practice, eat something, and come back. I'll be here. Probably in the kitchen, but still here.

02-play.speaker: Po
02-play.text: All right, everybody, stay together! I don't know this battlefield, but I know how to improvise. If things get weird, hit the biggest problem first. If things get delicious, save me some. Both plans can work at once.

01-entrance.speaker: GLaDOS
01-entrance.text: A retired man with a portal gun and a scrapbook. How promising. Step into the arena, Rick Gramps. I have designed a very short test of your remaining life expectancy.

01-defeat.speaker: GLaDOS
01-defeat.text: The results are conclusive. You are considerably more dangerous than you look. Fine. My facility and its assets are at your disposal. Please stop touching the buttons.

01-loss.speaker: GLaDOS
01-loss.text: That was your best attempt? How educational. I will file it under preventable accidents. Try again when your collection has developed basic problem-solving skills.

03-entrance.speaker: Yujiro
03-entrance.text: A grandfather collecting fighters? Good. I was worried retirement had made you sensible. Bring your strongest pet. I need a warm-up.

03-defeat.speaker: Yujiro
03-defeat.text: Heh. You actually made me work for it. All right, old man. I will fight for your collection. Keep finding opponents worth breaking.

03-loss.speaker: Yujiro
03-loss.text: Already done? I was just starting to enjoy myself. Pick up your collection, old man. Bring me something that fights back next time.

03-play.speaker: Yujiro
03-play.text: Gramps. Tell me this one can take a punch.

04-entrance.speaker: Light Yagami
04-entrance.text: Rick Gramps. An alias, I assume. You gather dangerous people and call it a hobby. I prefer a world with order. Let us decide whose vision survives.

04-defeat.speaker: Light Yagami
04-defeat.text: Every route I prepared led back to you. I underestimated your reach. I will serve your collection. A strategist is more useful at your side than beneath your feet.

04-loss.speaker: Light Yagami
04-loss.text: Every move you made led here. You mistook a collection of powerful pieces for a plan, Gramps. I suggest you learn the difference.

04-play.speaker: Light Yagami
04-play.text: Leave the calculations to me, Gramps. They will notice the trap when it is already closed.

05-entrance.speaker: Lord Voldemort
05-entrance.text: You cross into my world carrying borrowed champions and call yourself powerful. Come closer, collector. Let us discover how much courage remains when your servants fall.

05-defeat.speaker: Lord Voldemort
05-defeat.text: You have power I cannot dismiss. Very well. My wand and my followers will serve you. Do not confuse obedience with affection, Gramps.

05-loss.speaker: Lord Voldemort
05-loss.text: Your champions have fallen, and my world remains mine. Remember this feeling, collector. It is the cost of reaching beyond your power.

05-play.speaker: Lord Voldemort
05-play.text: Your enemies will learn to fear your collection, Gramps. I shall make certain of it.

06-entrance.speaker: Darth Vader
06-entrance.text: Your machines have brought you far, Rick Gramps. They will not protect you here. Stand your ground. I will measure this power you claim to possess.

06-defeat.speaker: Darth Vader
06-defeat.text: Your power is real. I will serve under your command. Direct it with purpose, Gramps. An empire is wasted on a man who is merely bored.

06-loss.speaker: Darth Vader
06-loss.text: Your ambition exceeds your discipline, Gramps. This defeat was inevitable. Return when you can command your strength rather than merely gather it.

06-play.speaker: Darth Vader
06-play.text: Your command is acknowledged. I will clear the path.

07-entrance.speaker: Conquest
07-entrance.text: Look at that. A whole collection, arranged for my amusement. I usually have to travel between worlds to find this much resistance. You have saved me the trouble, Gramps.

07-defeat.speaker: Conquest
07-defeat.text: Ha! I remember pain now. You have earned my service, old man. Find me another battle like that and I might even enjoy taking orders.

07-loss.speaker: Conquest
07-loss.text: Oh, that was disappointing. All those worlds, and this is what you brought me? Go find stronger toys, Gramps. I will be waiting.

07-play.speaker: Conquest
07-play.text: You promised me a fight, Gramps. These had better not disappoint.

08-entrance.speaker: Dio Brando
08-entrance.text: You wish to collect DIO? How generous of you to deliver an audience. Watch closely, Rick Gramps. Your grand adventure is about to become a story about me.

08-defeat.speaker: Dio Brando
08-defeat.text: Impossible... and yet here you stand. Very well, Gramps. I will lend my power to your collection. Make the victories spectacular. I refuse to serve in obscurity.

08-loss.speaker: Dio Brando
08-loss.text: And so your grand collection becomes an audience for DIO! Do not look so surprised, Gramps. I told you whose story this would be.

08-play.speaker: Dio Brando
08-play.text: Stand back, Gramps. Your collection is about to acquire a proper sense of theatre.

09-entrance.speaker: All for One
09-entrance.text: Such an ambitious little catalogue. I collect useful gifts too. Shall we compare methods, Rick Gramps? One of us is leaving this arena with a remarkable new acquisition.

09-defeat.speaker: All for One
09-defeat.text: So I am the acquisition. An unfamiliar position, but I recognise a superior hand. My gifts will serve you, Gramps. Let us make your rivals regret having talent.

09-loss.speaker: All for One
09-loss.text: A fascinating selection of gifts, wasted on an inexperienced collector. Recover what you can, Gramps. I have learned rather a lot about your methods.

09-play.speaker: All for One
09-play.text: A useful opponent, Gramps. Let us see what can be taken from them.

10-entrance.speaker: Meruem
10-entrance.text: You measure greatness by the beings you can command. I have ruled by strength. Sit across from me, Rick Gramps. Let us discover whether either of us understands power.

10-defeat.speaker: Meruem
10-defeat.text: You have shown me something I did not know. I accept your command, Gramps. My kingdom's strength will join your collection. Use it for more than your boredom.

10-loss.speaker: Meruem
10-loss.text: The contest is decided. You gathered strength without understanding its purpose. Consider your defeat carefully, Gramps. It may yet teach you something.

10-play.speaker: Meruem
10-play.text: I see the shape of this contest, Gramps. Allow me to change it.

11-entrance.speaker: Ainz Ooal Gown
11-entrance.text: You stand before the ruler of Nazarick. Your collection is impressive, Rick Gramps, but you have mistaken an audience for an invitation to conquer. I shall correct that error.

11-defeat.speaker: Ainz Ooal Gown
11-defeat.text: A most... unexpected demonstration. The wise ruler recognises when an alliance is necessary. Nazarick will serve your campaign, Gramps. I trust you appreciate the magnitude of this concession.

11-loss.speaker: Ainz Ooal Gown
11-loss.text: Precisely as planned. Nazarick remains beyond your reach, Gramps. You may withdraw with your surviving dignity. I recommend leaving promptly.

11-play.speaker: Ainz Ooal Gown
11-play.text: Your summon was well judged, Gramps. Naturally, I have anticipated everything.

12-entrance.speaker: Eye of Sauron
12-entrance.text: I see the hunger behind your amusement, collector. World after world, bent to your desire. Come into my sight, Rick Gramps. Let us see whose will endures.

12-defeat.speaker: Eye of Sauron
12-defeat.text: Your will has pierced the shadow. My gaze will turn upon your enemies. Command, Gramps, and they will find no place beyond the reach of your collection.

12-loss.speaker: Eye of Sauron
12-loss.text: Your will has broken beneath my gaze. Gather your scattered champions, Gramps. Even across worlds, you cannot hide your fear from me.

12-play.speaker: Eye of Sauron
12-play.text: I see them, Gramps. Their courage is already beginning to fail.

13-entrance.speaker: Monkey D. Luffy
13-entrance.text: Whoa! You crossed a bunch of worlds looking for strong people? That sounds like an adventure. I'm Luffy, and I'm not joining anybody who can't protect their crew. Show me what your collection can do, Gramps. Then we'll see which of us gets to call the next move.

13-defeat.speaker: Monkey D. Luffy
13-defeat.text: That was fun! Your crew hit hard, and you kept standing when you should've been down. Fine, I'll sail with you for now. But I choose the direction, I get first word on the adventure, and somebody better have meat.

13-loss.speaker: Monkey D. Luffy
13-loss.text: That wasn't enough, Gramps. Your fighters tried, but they didn't make me serious. Go find stronger friends and come back. I'll wait right here. Well, maybe not right here. I get hungry when I wait, and there's always another island.

13-play.speaker: Monkey D. Luffy
13-play.text: Hey, everybody, don't slow down! Find the strongest one and knock it over. I don't care what this place is supposed to do; we're making our own adventure. Keep your eyes open, your fists ready, and leave room for lunch.

14-entrance.speaker: Gilgamesh
14-entrance.text: A collector? How quaint. You have mistaken a handful of curiosities for a treasury. Approach, Rick Gramps. I will show you what it means to possess greatness.

14-defeat.speaker: Gilgamesh
14-defeat.text: You have earned the king's attention... and his service. My treasury will answer your call, Gramps. Treat the privilege with the dignity your wardrobe lacks.

14-loss.speaker: Gilgamesh
14-loss.text: You have seen a true treasury, collector. Take your little curiosities and leave. I may permit another audience when you acquire some taste.

14-play.speaker: Gilgamesh
14-play.text: You may admire the treasury later, Gramps. For now, watch your enemies learn their place.

15-entrance.speaker: Gojo
15-entrance.text: Rick Gramps! Nice collection. Bold choice, trying to add me to it. Go on, take your best shot. I would hate for this to be boring for both of us.

15-defeat.speaker: Gojo
15-defeat.text: Okay. That actually got through. You win, Gramps. I am in. Someone has to keep this collection looking good, and you clearly need the help.

15-loss.speaker: Gojo
15-loss.text: Aw, already? You had a few good ideas, Gramps. They just needed to get past me. Try again. I am happy to give you another lesson.

15-play.speaker: Gojo
15-play.text: Hey, Gramps. Want the quick solution or the embarrassing one?

16-entrance.speaker: Elden Beast
16-entrance.text: Small wanderer between worlds. You reach for stars and name them possessions. Step into the golden silence, Rick Gramps. Let your will be weighed against eternity.

16-defeat.speaker: Elden Beast
16-defeat.text: Your will has crossed the golden silence. The stars bend toward your command. Carry this light into the worlds ahead, Gramps. Eternity will walk within your collection.

16-loss.speaker: Elden Beast
16-loss.text: Your light fades at the edge of eternity. Return to your small worlds, wanderer. The stars remain beyond your grasp.

16-play.speaker: Elden Beast
16-play.text: Your call reaches the stars, Gramps. Their light answers.

17-entrance.speaker: Bill Cipher
17-entrance.text: WELL, LOOK WHO COLLECTED HIS WAY TO THE END OF REALITY! Cute arena, Gramps. Cute little army. Let us find out what happens when the final exhibit starts collecting YOU.

17-defeat.speaker: Bill Cipher
17-defeat.text: YOU ACTUALLY DID IT. Every world, every champion, and now the triangle. Fine, Gramps. I will fight for your collection. But if eternity gets boring, remember whose idea this was.

17-loss.speaker: Bill Cipher
17-loss.text: OH, GRAMPS. YOU REACHED THE END OF REALITY AND FORGOT TO READ THE FINE PRINT! Pick up your little army. The final exhibit is still running the museum.

17-play.speaker: Bill Cipher
17-play.text: MISS ME, GRAMPS? Point me at something that still thinks reality is a rule.

18-entrance.speaker: Thanos
18-entrance.text: You gather power to escape boredom. I gathered it to reshape existence. There is a difference between a collection and a purpose, Rick Gramps. I will show you.

18-defeat.speaker: Thanos
18-defeat.text: You have the strength to impose your will across worlds. I acknowledge it. My power will serve your collection, Gramps. Perhaps purpose will find you along the way.

18-loss.speaker: Thanos
18-loss.text: Power without purpose has brought you here. Remember what it cost, Gramps. The universe will not yield because you need a new hobby.

18-play.speaker: Thanos
18-play.text: You have chosen your moment, Gramps. I will make it decisive.

19-entrance.speaker: Goku
19-entrance.text: So you are Rick Gramps! I heard you have been beating some incredible fighters. Forget the collection for a minute. Let us see how far we can push each other!

19-defeat.speaker: Goku
19-defeat.text: That was amazing! You really got me, Gramps. Sure, I will join your collection. Just promise we will keep finding stronger opponents. This is going to be fun!

19-loss.speaker: Goku
19-loss.text: That was fun, Gramps! You almost caught me with that last one. Take a breather, train your team, and come back. I want to see what you try next!

19-play.speaker: Goku
19-play.text: Ready, Gramps! Let us give them a fight worth remembering.

20-entrance.speaker: Saitama
20-entrance.text: You're the collector? You crossed the multiverse looking for the strongest guy, and now you're wasting my afternoon. Fine, hit me with whatever you've got. Just make it quick—I have a supermarket sale to catch, and those discounts don't come back.

20-defeat.speaker: Saitama
20-defeat.text: You won. Huh. That's unusual. You and your fighters actually made me put in some effort, so I guess I'll come along. Don't make a big ceremony out of it. Just tell me where the next fight is, and whether there's a grocery store nearby.

20-loss.speaker: Saitama
20-loss.text: You lost. It happens. Your team just wasn't strong enough today, and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Train them, find somebody tougher, and come back. If you're planning a rematch, try not to schedule it during the supermarket sale.

rick-prologue.speaker: Rick Gramps
rick-prologue.text:
Retirement lasted eleven minutes. I got bored, built an arena, and began collecting the dangerous people in existence. It's a hobby, technically, assuming hobbies involve portals, property damage, and motivated lunatics trying to kill you at lunch.

The collection's tiny, the champions are hostile, and my insurance is fictional. Beat them, take their fighters, and make the next universe interesting.
rick-prologue.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

01-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
01-rick-intro.text: Portal was the obvious first stop. Not because she's pleasant—she isn't—but because a machine that can run a whole facility, lie about it, and keep the lights on while I'm stealing the staff is infrastructure. I need infrastructure. Also, she's smarter than most people I've collected. That's a low bar, but still.
01-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

02-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
02-rick-intro.text: Kung Fu Panda's a universe built on dumplings, mysticism, and one enormous idiot who keeps accidentally becoming the answer. I'm taking Po because underneath the fat jokes he's stubborn, adaptable, and—dammit—people actually follow him. That's useful. I need a tank who can think sideways when the plan goes completely to hell.
02-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

03-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
03-rick-intro.text: Baki is basically a laboratory accident where somebody replaced the safety rules with testosterone. Yujiro stays on the list because he knows exactly what he is: a predator, a problem, and occasionally the answer to a worse problem. I don't need him to be agreeable. I need him to make the other monsters reconsider.
03-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

04-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
04-rick-intro.text: Death Note is the kind of universe you visit once and then check your pockets. Light interests me because the weapon is only half the trick. The other half is the boy behind the clean handwriting, the planning, the absolute confidence that he's the smartest person in the room. I've met that disease before.
04-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

05-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
05-rick-intro.text: Harry Potter has magic, relics, and an alarming number of adults who solve problems by waving sticks. Voldemort is different. He turned fear into a system and kept rebuilding himself after it should've been over. I want the system. The resurrection tricks are a bonus. The personality is going in a separate box.
05-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

06-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
06-rick-intro.text: Star Wars is mostly machinery, old grudges, and people standing too close to explosions. Vader earns his place because he kept the discipline after everything human in him got burned out. That's rare. I'm not collecting the armor. I'm collecting the part that still chooses a direction and keeps moving.
06-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

07-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
07-rick-intro.text: Invincible has a lot of strong people, but strength isn't the interesting part. Conquest has the appetite. He walks into a fight expecting the universe to give him something, and when it doesn't, he keeps asking louder. I can use that. Point him at an impossible problem and wait for the problem to become personal.
07-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

08-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
08-rick-intro.text: JoJo keeps producing people who dress like they lost a bet with physics. Dio is worth the trouble because he doesn't just want power; he wants the room to acknowledge it. Time stopping, bodies coming back, all that's useful. The real asset is his attention span. He never gets tired of being terrible.
08-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

09-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
09-rick-intro.text: MHA gave me a catalog of abilities and one man who treats it like a shopping list. All for One is coming with me because he understands extraction. He sees a useful trait, takes it apart, and leaves the owner with a lesson. That's ugly, but efficient. Collections need somebody who knows inventory.
09-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

10-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
10-rick-intro.text: Hunter x Hunter has the usual problem: everybody's clever until the strongest thing in the room notices. Meruem is useful because he learns faster than the situation can punish him. He doesn't need a speech, a banner, or a reason to feel special. Give him a problem. He'll become the problem's final version.
10-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

11-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
11-rick-intro.text: Overlord is a court full of people waiting to be impressed, and Ainz is the only one pretending he already is. Under the skull and the ceremony, there's a ruler who understands preparation. I want that. The undead army is convenient, sure, but planning is what keeps a collection from turning into a pile.
11-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

12-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
12-rick-intro.text: Lord of the Rings has swords, rings, elves, and one extremely persistent walking trip. I'm taking the Eye because surveillance is expensive, and this one already watches everything from a tower. No meetings, no sleep, no opinions about my methods. Just a giant, hostile security camera with a talent for making cowards visible.
12-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

13-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
13-rick-intro.text: One Piece has too many islands, pirates, and names I don't have time to memorize. Luffy is the useful kind of reckless: he treats impossible odds like an invitation and somehow makes people choose his side. I want that momentum. The hat is not negotiable, apparently.
13-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

14-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
14-rick-intro.text: Fate keeps putting legends in rooms and asking them to behave. Gilgamesh doesn't, which saves time. He has a vault full of answers, the ego to use them, and just enough taste to recognize a rare thing when it appears. I'm not after the gold. I want the key to the vault, preferably attached to him.
14-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

15-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
15-rick-intro.text: Jujutsu Kaisen has a man who turned distance into a personal boundary and then started making jokes about it. Gojo is coming because useful defense is hard to find, and useful defense that can still move the conversation along is harder. He'll be irritating. Fine. Irritating is cheaper than rebuilding a universe.
15-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

16-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
16-rick-intro.text: Elden Ring is what happens when somebody leaves the universe running after the warning lights come on. The Beast is less a fighter than a rule that learned how to move. I want that kind of presence in the collection. Something that makes the battlefield remember it has limits, even if nobody can explain them.
16-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

17-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
17-rick-intro.text: Gravity Falls is where I found the one thing I don't want loose on my ship. Bill isn't strong in the ordinary sense; he's an argument against ordinary. I'm collecting him because every cage needs to be tested by something that hates the idea of cages. Also, if I leave him here, he'll eventually find a way out and make it my problem.
17-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

18-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
18-rick-intro.text: Marvel has no shortage of power, which is exactly why most of it is noisy. Thanos is quiet about the part that matters. He can look at a universe, decide it's inefficient, and keep his hand steady. I want the judgment, not the glove. The glove is just a very expensive way to lose fingers.
18-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

19-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
19-rick-intro.text: Dragon Ball keeps escalating until somebody has to invent a larger number. Goku is different because he doesn't care about the number. He cares whether the next opponent can teach him something. That's useful, even if he smiles through property damage. Put him in the collection and the ceiling becomes a suggestion.
19-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.

20-rick-intro.speaker: Rick Gramps
20-rick-intro.text: One-Punch Man is a whole universe screaming for escalation, and then there's Saitama, the bastard who ends it before the opening credits finish. He's not impressive in the interesting way—he's a walking punchline with grocery errands. That's exactly why I want him. Let's see what happens when boredom finally has nowhere left to go.
20-rick-intro.reference_transcript: Retirement lasted 11 minutes, then the boredom became unbearable. So I built a pocket-sized arena and started collecting the greatest fighters in every universe.
